content.text: Everything builds and vets cleanly, and the binary runs correctly on Linux (`Linux 6.8.0-139-generic (x86_64)`).

Module set up:

- **`go.mod`** — module `syscli`, `golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0` as the only dependency (this is the standard way to reach syscalls the stdlib doesn't expose — `unix.Uname`, `unix.Sysctl`, `windows.RtlGetNtVersionNumbers`, etc.).
- **`sysinfo/`** — one file per OS (`sysinfo_linux.go`, `sysinfo_darwin.go`, `sysinfo_windows.go`), each with a matching build constraint via the `_GOOS.go` filename suffix, so only the right one compiles per target.
- **`main.go`** — calls `sysinfo.Get()` and prints the result.

Verified: builds for `linux/amd64`, `darwin/arm64`, and `windows/amd64` via `GOOS`/`GOARCH` cross-compilation, `go vet` is clean, `gofmt` reports no diffs, and the Linux binary runs correctly (`Linux 6.8.0-139-generic (x86_64)`).

To add more syscalls later, just extend the relevant per-OS file (or add new ones the same way) — `x/sys/unix` and `x/sys/windows` cover the vast majority of platform-specific calls.

- **`sysinfo/`** — one file per OS (`sysinfo_linux.go`, `sysinfo_darwin.go`, `sysinfo_windows.go`), each with a matching build constraint via the `_GOOS.go` filename suffix, so only the right one compiles per target.
- **`main.go`** — calls `sysinfo.Get()` and prints the result.
